technical_and_design_decisions: Will use Spring Boot as the base framework for all modules and microservices, leveraging its auto-configuration and dependency management.
For Kafka integration (U1, U4), will use Spring Kafka with customized serializers/deserializers via property-driven encoder/decoder configuration.
For gpfdist sink (U2) and gpload tasklet (U6), will implement as Spring Cloud Data Flow modules using Spring Batch and custom tasklets, communicating via HTTP to Greenplum components.
UI infrastructure (U3) will integrate Admin UI and Flo by setting up an Angular frontend with REST APIs provided by the existing Spring XD/SCDF backend.
For efficient file reading (U5), will implement a Spring Batch Tasklet that uses FileChannel or memory-mapped I/O to process files without loading entire content into memory.
To decouple Hadoop dependencies (U7), will restructure the Maven/Gradle build to move Hadoop-specific JARs to optional runtime dependencies and use reflection for classloading.

Dynamic classpath for modules (U8) will be implemented by extending the module classloader to accept a configurable classpath string, parsing it at runtime to load additional JARs from specified locations.
All code will be developed in Java 17+, with unit tests using JUnit 5 and Mockito, and integration tests using Testcontainers where necessary.
assumptions: The developer is proficient in the Spring ecosystem, Java, and build tools (Maven/Gradle).
The existing Spring XD codebase is available and functional; the work is an increment on top of it.
The environment for development (IDE, build tools, test infrastructure) is already set up.
No external dependencies beyond those specified (e.g., Greenplum, Kafka) need to be installed; mock or embedded versions are acceptable for testing.
The UI infrastructure (U3) assumes that the Admin UI and Flo are separate projects that can be included as dependencies without major modifications.
All effort estimates include analysis, design, coding, unit testing, integration testing, and documentation for each activity.
Effort for code reviews, deployment, and non-functional tasks (e.g., CI pipeline setup) is excluded.
The most likely effort estimates assume no major unforeseen issues; typical productivity levels apply.

activities.activity_description: Implement the ability to configure custom encoders and decoders (serializers/deserializers) for Kafka source, sink, and bus modules in Spring XD. This includes extending configuration, creating SPI for user-provided classes, and updating documentation.

Develop an out-of-the-box gpfdist sink module that writes data to Greenplum/HAWQ via the gpfdist fast data movement protocol. Implementation includes a Spring Cloud Data Flow module, HTTP client integration, error handling, and unit/integration tests.

activities.activity_name: Setup UI Infrastructure for Admin UI and Flo (U3)
activities.activity_description: Set up the infrastructure to integrate the Admin UI and Flo components into the Spring XD/SCDF project. This involves configuring the frontend build pipeline, connecting to backend APIs, and ensuring compatibility with the existing backend.

Create a complete end-to-end demonstration/example of Kafka integration with Spring XD, including producer, stream, and consumer. This serves as a verification and study tool for performance and scalability.

Implement a tasklet-based approach for reading files efficiently (e.g., using memory-mapped I/O or streaming) without loading the entire file into memory. Compare with the stream-based approach and provide a configurable option.

Develop a gpload tasklet that ingests data from various sources into Greenplum/HAWQ efficiently. This includes integration with the gpload utility, parameter configuration, error handling, and testing.

activities.activity_name: Remove Hadoop Dependencies from Root Classpath (U7)
activities.activity_description: Refactor the project to decouple Hadoop dependencies from the root classpath, so they are only loaded when needed (e.g., when using HDFS as module registry). This involves moving JARs to optional dependencies and using dynamic classloading.

Add support for a configurable dynamic classpath for modules, allowing users to specify additional JARs via module options or properties (e.g., based on distribution or provider). Implementation includes parsing classpath strings and loading classes at runtime.

Perform overall integration testing across all implemented features, fix cross-cutting issues, and prepare the increment for release. This includes running the full test suite, verifying compatibility, and updating release notes.
Set up any required project configuration (e.g., build files, CI pipeline adjustments) and produce comprehensive documentation for the new features, including user guides and API references.
